title: Draft Gmail replies with AI and send them yourself
h1: draft gmail replies with ai, then send them yourself
description: Have a bot write Gmail drafts in your voice, in the right thread, with attachments. What it needs, what it can't do, and a routine to copy.
answer: a bot can save a reply into your gmail drafts, in the same thread as the email it answers, with any attachment it needs, and your gmail signature if the connection can read it. nothing is sent: the draft waits in gmail for you to read, edit and send. it's a gentle way to hand email to ai: a bad draft just sits there until you delete it.

review.by: lead agent, against Metal docs and the composio gmail catalog

og_line: replies in your drafts, sent by you.
what:
**it writes the email and parks it in your drafts. you press send.** it can file the draft inside the right conversation, add people on cc, attach a file and add your signature.

if it can't find the thread you meant, gmail still saves the draft, just as a new email. worth knowing when you go looking for it.
uses: answer the three clients who wrote overnight, so you just read and send
turn your call notes into a follow-up with the agreed next steps
reply to a supplier with the invoice attached from their last email
write a polite "no" to an invitation for you to soften or send

routine.message: every weekday at 9, look at emails from people at @acme.com that came in since yesterday and still have no reply from me. for each one, read the whole thread and save a short reply in my gmail drafts, in that thread, leaving the subject empty so it stays in the thread, in my voice: friendly, no exclamation marks, sign off with just my first name. then tell me here which drafts you made, one line each. never send anything.
routine.needs: gmail connected, with read and write access for this bot
routine.output:
3 drafts in gmail

1. dana (acme): re: q3 quote, says we can do the 15th.
2. lee (acme): re: invoice 1042, attached the corrected pdf.
3. omar (acme): re: kickoff, proposes tuesday or wednesday at 10.

nothing sent.

steps: connect gmail in **Connected apps** with read and write for this bot. drafting is a change, so read only won't do.
tell it how you write, once: "short, warm, no exclamation marks, first name only". it keeps that in **Memory**.
ask for one draft, read it in gmail, fix what's off ("shorter", "don't apologise").
once two or three come back right, turn it into a routine like the one above.
watch: no thread found? it saves a new email with the subject you gave it.
if the bot gives a reply its own subject, gmail starts a new conversation. ask it to leave the subject blank for replies.
a draft has your name on it. read before you send.
it doesn't know what you said on a call. tell it once and it keeps a note.

faq.q: will it send the draft by itself?
faq.a: no. this action only saves a draft. sending is a different action; it asks you first by default, unless you set a daily amount or the bot is on **Full access** with no sending rule.

faq.q: can it reply inside the same gmail thread?
faq.a: yes. it reads the thread and saves the draft into it, so it shows as a reply. if the thread can't be found, the draft is saved as a new email.
it can. tell it to include your gmail signature, the one set up under send mail as in gmail's settings. if the connection can't read that setting, the signature is skipped, so check the sign-off.

sources.label: Metal docs: a bot's computer, asking first

steps: connect gmail with read and write
ask: "draft a reply to dana's last email, two lines"
open your drafts and read it
say what to fix; it remembers

worked.before:
from: lee (acme)
"the total on invoice 1042 looks wrong, can you check?"
worked.after:
draft, in the same thread:
"hi lee, you're right, we doubled the shipping. corrected invoice attached. sorry about that.
maya"

waiting in drafts. nothing sent.

mistakes.fix: saving a draft is a change. it needs read and write for gmail.
three lines about how you write beat ten corrections later.
